mutated_contract.problem: Beyond skills, isolation, output schema and scripts, the native call to renderTaskPrompt omits three further inputs the legacy runner supplies, and each is a real loss rather than a legacy-only concept. First, completedBlockers: runner.ts passes the resolved blockers so their contracts render as dependency context; native passes none, so a child never sees what unblocked it. Native reads neither the error nor the mandatoryRules metadata, so it takes the third option nobody chose: launch silently missing its rules and emit no mandatory_rules_injection meta.

mutated_contract.problem: A specialists job identity reached substrate session columns on XTRM-379 seq1: issue_journal.session_id=<redacted> with run_id='job-122c14', and execution_bindings.session_id=<redacted> with activation_id='job-122c14'. The original contract assumed an untraced producer emitted this shape. The trace disproved that premise. Evidence: (1) no code in the specialists repo or its installed dist composes a `job-<id>` identity - the native activation host mints `act:<uuid12>` (src/activation/native-host.ts:956; identical at the revision live at the time, f526de0f:src/activation/native-host.ts:407); (2) the settlement publication passes only `sessionId: subject.piSessionId` and never assigns runId, and it always sets ctx.actor (src/activation/settlement-publication.ts:629, :178) - the historic journal envelope has NO actor leg and DOES carry runId, so publication is disproven as the writer; (3) provenance.dispatch accepts no --run flag while journal.append does (cli/sb.ts flag tables), so the two columns came from two separate CLI calls; (4) the closures for XTRM-379 record actor 'sb-cli' with reasons describing a manual live settlement verification of explorer job 122c14. The writer was therefore caller-supplied CLI identity typed by hand during a live verification, not a producer code path. What remains true and unfenced is the durable guarantee: nothing pinned that the historic shape cannot be written again.

packages/substrate/docs (corrected trace statement where the specialists publication path is described)

mutated_contract.problem:
`issue_journal` stores execution identity on every row it can, and every read path throws it away.

Measured on the live board (`~/.xtrm/state.db`, 1397 journal rows): `participant_id` populated 996 times, `session_id` 78, `activation_id` 73, `run_id` 1, `execution_context_json` 78.

Demonstrated loss: `SPECIALISTS-106` journal seq2 has, in the database, `participant_id='specialist::executor'`, `activation_id='act:23b2212a-c44'`, `session_id=<redacted> Reading that same entry through the CLI:

  `sb journal show SPECIALISTS-106 --json`

returns an entry with exactly ten keys - `createdAt, hasMechanical, hasSemantic, id, issueRevision, kind, mechanical, result, semantic, sequence`. No `participantId`, no `activationId`, no `sessionId`, no `runId`, no `executionContext`. The human view shows only a `summary:` line.

The columns are selected and then discarded in the read projection, so the loss is at render/projection time, not at capture time. Consequence: the journal is continuity, and a future agent reading why an entry exists cannot see which session or Specialist produced it, even when the answer is on the row.

mutated_contract.problem:
xt claude launches a Claude Code session but does not enable the specialists plugin's Channel wake, so a dispatched specialist that settles cannot push a notification into the launched session. Proven live on 2026-09-12: with the plugin installed and XTRM_SUBSTRATE_DIR set, a dispatch settles and the session is woken ONLY by the asyncRewake polling hook. When the session is additionally launched with a channels flag, Claude Code registers the channel and the settle pushes `notifications/claude/channel` carrying `Specialist explorer: completed (act:...)`, which renders in-session as `<- specialists: ...`. xt provides no way to get that, so every xt-launched session falls back to the slow polling path.

A second, independent defect found in the same test: xt claude does NOT propagate the caller's environment into the launched session. Exporting XTRM_SUBSTRATE_DIR before `xt claude` produced an empty value inside the session (`ENV=[]`), and specialist_dispatch was refused with work_item_store_unavailable. The value only arrived when injected with `tmux new-window -e`. Without XTRM_SUBSTRATE_DIR, dispatch does not work at all from an xt-launched session.
scope: The xt claude launcher in cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts and whatever composes its argv and tmux environment.
Documentation of the required managed-settings keys.

constraints: (a) and (b) ship TOGETHER in one change. A range alone relocates the silent cliff from patch releases to minor releases rather than removing it: a 0.7.0 release would still fail closed with the whole surface gone and only a warning. 0.6.1 sat for months because nothing surfaced the drift, not because the comparison was equality.

Comparator semantics, general caret rule, not a 0.x special case: major>0 same major and installed>=baseline; major==0, minor>0 same minor and installed>=baseline; 0.0.x exact match; prerelease or unparseable on either side is NOT compatible and must carry a diagnostic reason. Fail closed and say why; never silently treat it as a match.
The comparator is pure: no filesystem access, no installed package, so it is testable without the environment.
Keep the change small enough to review as a diff.
nonGoals: Do NOT decouple the hard deny from extension health. This was proposed and REJECTED on evidence: the manifest field is literally `denied_natives_when_extension`, GITNEXUS_HARD_DENY_TOOLS is exactly {grep,find,ls}, and the native READ_ONLY tier already grants [read,grep,find,ls]. All three tests are read-only and already granted at the lowest tier, so the rule is a substitution ('graph-first instead of text search'), not a security boundary, and restoring them costs no security. The defect is the false negative - a working 0.6.4 classified unhealthy - not the coupling.

Do NOT add a `compatible_range` catalog field yet. `version` keeps exactly its current meaning ('the build these tools were verified against'), every existing reader sees it unchanged, and the rule is derived in the comparator. Add the field only when a catalog needs a NON-caret rule, at which point it carries information the derivation cannot.
Do NOT add a semver dependency. `semver` is present at 7.7.4 only transitively and importing it undeclared is fragile; a ~15-line general caret comparator covers the case.

Do NOT add a unit test that resolves against the INSTALLED extension. That is machine-dependent and is the SPECIALISTS-24 defect class (three tests that failed depending on whether Substrate was linked). The guard belongs in doctor/CI.
Do NOT change specialist configs, the catalog contents, or the shape of ResolvedToolContract.

mutated_contract.problem: Catalog version pins are enforced by exact string equality at two runtime sites: src/pi/session.ts:290 (gitnexus) and src/pi/session.ts:346 (python-kernel). On mismatch each returns loaded_unhealthy with catalogCompatible false; resolveEffectiveExtensionState (src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts:127) maps that to includeTools false, and resolveManifestTools (:177-184) drops every tool that catalog contributes, emitting only a warning string. src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts:97 performs the same equality comparison independently, so the diagnostics surface and the runtime gate are two implementations of one rule that must not drift. Root cause: an identity check is standing in for a compatibility check. The gate is purely static - it reads package.json's version field and never loads the extension and never verifies that any tool name the catalog advertises actually exists. So loaded_healthy asserts nothing about capability, and a patch release of an independently-versioned extension silently erases a whole capability surface. This is not hypothetical: the gitnexus pin sat at 0.6.1 from a May executor checkpoint (8bf4c6f5) while 0.6.2, 0.6.3 and 0.6.4 all shipped, and every gitnexus tool was invisible on both runtimes until SPECIALISTS-32 bumped it. Recurrence is structural: the extension releases on its own cadence and nothing guards the pin. The one test that referenced the pin, tests/unit/specialist/tool-catalog.test.ts:51, asserted the literal '0.6.1' - it enforced the stale value rather than catching it, and it now asserts '0.6.4', which will lock in the next stale value identically. CONCLUSION REACHED JOINTLY with specialists-xt-claude-i1q2, who reviewed the reading against origin/master ceb6be28. One proposed remedy was REJECTED on evidence and the rejection is recorded under NON_GOALS so it is not re-proposed. A third catalog pin was examined and is a DIFFERENT finding: service-knowledge has no runtime gate at all - src/pi/session.ts:399-402 supplies extensionState for gitnexus and python-kernel only - so it resolves through resolveEffectiveExtensionState(undefined) to 'available' unconditionally, unverified, while its source_tiers are empty at every tier so no tool can be dropped. That is a pin nothing validates, not a silent tool drop, and it is recorded as a separate sub-observation rather than folded into the primary defect.
scope: The shared comparator: caret-of-baseline compatibility, derived from the catalog's existing `version` field, in one place used by all three call sites.
src/pi/session.ts:290 (gitnexus) and src/pi/session.ts:346 (python-kernel): replace `installedVersion !== catalog.version` with the comparator.
src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts:97: same comparator, so diagnostics report the same verdict the runtime gate reaches.
Admission visibility: surface downgradeReasons at admission the way the build-staleness line is already surfaced, instead of leaving it as a warning inside the contract string.
Post-load verification: assert the promised tool names exist in the runtime registry at session_start in config/pi-extensions/extension-tool-policy/index.mjs (which already calls pi.getAllTools()).
tests/unit/specialist/tool-catalog.test.ts:51: assert that the pin satisfies the rule rather than asserting a literal version string.
A doctor/CI guard that compares the pin against the installed extension version, so it cannot silently drift for months again.

A range alone relocates the silent cliff from patch releases to minor releases rather than removing it: a 0.7.0 release would still fail closed with the whole surface gone and only a warning. 0.6.1 sat for months because nothing surfaced the drift, not because the comparison was equality.

Comparator semantics, general caret rule, not a 0.x special case: major>0 same major and installed>=baseline; major==0, minor>0 same minor and installed>=baseline; 0.0.x exact match; prerelease or unparseable on either side is NOT compatible and must carry a diagnostic reason. Fail closed and say why; never silently treat it as a match.
The comparator is pure: no filesystem access, no installed package, so it is testable without the environment.
Keep the change small enough to review as a diff.
nonGoals: Do NOT decouple the hard deny from extension health. This was proposed and REJECTED on evidence: the manifest field is literally `denied_natives_when_extension`, GITNEXUS_HARD_DENY_TOOLS is exactly {grep,find,ls}, and the native READ_ONLY tier already grants [read,grep,find,ls]. All three tests are read-only and already granted at the lowest tier, so the rule is a substitution ('graph-first instead of text search'), not a security boundary, and restoring them costs no security. The defect is the false negative - a working 0.6.4 classified unhealthy - not the coupling.

Do NOT add a `compatible_range` catalog field yet. `version` keeps exactly its current meaning ('the build these tools were verified against'), every existing reader sees it unchanged, and the rule is derived in the comparator. Add the field only when a catalog needs a NON-caret rule, at which point it carries information the derivation cannot.
Do NOT add a semver dependency. `semver` is present at 7.7.4 only transitively and importing it undeclared is fragile; a ~15-line general caret comparator covers the case.

Do NOT add a unit test that resolves against the INSTALLED extension. That is machine-dependent and is the SPECIALISTS-24 defect class (three tests that failed depending on whether Substrate was linked). The guard belongs in doctor/CI.
Do NOT change specialist configs, the catalog contents, or the shape of ResolvedToolContract.

output.artifact: Commits on a fix branch, a journal entry quoting the before/after resolution for both an in-range and an out-of-range version, and a PR.

mutated_contract.problem: Catalog version pins are enforced by exact string equality at two runtime sites: src/pi/session.ts:290 (gitnexus) and src/pi/session.ts:346 (python-kernel). On mismatch each returns loaded_unhealthy with catalogCompatible false; resolveEffectiveExtensionState (src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts:127) maps that to includeTools false, and resolveManifestTools (:177-184) drops every tool that catalog contributes, emitting only a warning string. src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts:97 performs the same equality comparison independently, so the diagnostics surface and the runtime gate are two implementations of one rule that must not drift. Root cause: an identity check is standing in for a compatibility check. The gate is purely static - it reads package.json's version field and never loads the extension and never verifies that any tool name the catalog advertises actually exists. So loaded_healthy asserts nothing about capability, and a patch release of an independently-versioned extension silently erases a whole capability surface. This is not hypothetical: the gitnexus pin sat at 0.6.1 from a May executor checkpoint (8bf4c6f5) while 0.6.2, 0.6.3 and 0.6.4 all shipped, and every gitnexus tool was invisible on both runtimes until SPECIALISTS-32 bumped it. Recurrence is structural: the extension releases on its own cadence and nothing guards the pin. The one test that referenced the pin, tests/unit/specialist/tool-catalog.test.ts:51, asserted the literal '0.6.1' - it enforced the stale value rather than catching it, and it now asserts '0.6.4', which will lock in the next stale value identically. CONCLUSION REACHED JOINTLY with specialists-xt-claude-i1q2, who reviewed the reading against origin/master ceb6be28. One proposed remedy was REJECTED on evidence and the rejection is recorded under NON_GOALS so it is not re-proposed. A third catalog pin was examined and is a DIFFERENT finding: service-knowledge has no runtime gate at all - src/pi/session.ts:399-402 supplies extensionState for gitnexus and python-kernel only - so it resolves through resolveEffectiveExtensionState(undefined) to 'available' unconditionally, unverified, while its source_tiers are empty at every tier so no tool can be dropped. That is a pin nothing validates, not a silent tool drop, and it is recorded as a separate sub-observation rather than folded into the primary defect.
scope: The relevant code and tests.
mutated_contract.success: One shared comparator decides catalog compatibility, and all three call sites use it, so the runtime gate and the diagnostics classifier can never disagree. A version inside the compatible range resolves healthy with no warning; a version outside it fails with a named reason rather than a bare 'loaded_unhealthy'. The failure is visible at admission, so a coordinator cannot silently receive a reduced capability surface. After a session starts, the tools the catalog promised are asserted to exist in the runtime registry, so a genuine capability change is caught by the thing that actually matters. A guard fails when the installed version falls outside the pin's range, so drift cannot ship unnoticed again.

validation.check: Table-driven pure unit test over the comparator: (0.6.3 vs baseline 0.6.4) incompatible, (0.6.5 vs 0.6.4) compatible, (0.7.0 vs 0.6.4) incompatible, (1.9.0 vs 1.2.0) compatible, (2.0.0 vs 1.9.0) incompatible, (1.2.0 vs 1.9.0) incompatible as a downgrade, prerelease on either side incompatible with a named reason, unparseable incompatible with a named reason.
A test proving all three call sites reach the same verdict for the same input, so the runtime gate and resolution-diagnostics cannot drift apart.
The full suite passes: bun --bun vitest run, plus bun run lint and bun run build with dist committed.
Live: a version inside the range resolves healthy with no downgrade reason; an out-of-range version reports a named reason at admission rather than a bare loaded_unhealthy.

mutated_contract.problem: Catalog version pins are enforced by exact string equality at two runtime sites: src/pi/session.ts:290 (gitnexus) and src/pi/session.ts:346 (python-kernel). One proposed remedy was REJECTED on evidence and the rejection is recorded under NON_GOALS so it is not re-proposed. constraints: The exclusion MUST key per (activation, attempt), NOT by the plain worktree path. leasePath derives from workspaceKey(workspace), which hashes realpath(workspace.worktreePath) (workspace-lease.ts:188-198), so a distinct key means passing a synthetic worktreePath; realpathSync fails on it and the literal is hashed, which is correct. A plain-workspace key would couple settlement publication to unrelated workspace mutability: a READ-ONLY activation holds no workspace lease, but it DOES publish settlements, so keying by workspace path would block it behind any unrelated write activation in the same worktree.

Ordering fact confirmed, so there is no self-collision to design around: every publish is preceded by releaseIfWriter (native-host.ts:1430 before :1493; :1522 before :1546; :1561 before :1585). The workspace lease is free at publication time in all three terminal paths.
On contention publishSettlement must DEGRADE to `pending` with the reason, never block and never throw - it returns through the same degraded path that already exists.
nonGoals: Writing a new lock or locking primitive - this repo already has one with the required properties (atomic linkSync/EEXIST publish, /proc/<pid>/stat field-22 startTicks liveness, 'uncertain' rather than a blind free)
Changing the publish ordering or the workspace lease lifecycle
Making publication blocking: publishSettlement is best-effort by contract and must never alter the validated activation result (ADR §38)

mutated_contract.problem: The SPECIALISTS-54 republish path is NOT exactly-once across processes. Two independent sequences produce a second WorkReceipt for one ExecutionBinding and a second Journal result for one (activation, attempt). Neither is reachable from the unit tests, because those doubles are single-threaded and the guard they defeat is a per-process boolean. D1: republishOncePerProcess guards with `this.republished`, a per-INSTANCE boolean (native-host.ts:389, :1327-1328), while the settlement store is a FILE store keyed by cwd (native-host.ts:425).
